Reference / http/xmlrpc

http/xmlrpc#

XML-RPC over HTTP: values, calls, a client and a handler.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let rpc = XmlRpcClient(origin: HttpClient(), endpoint: ParsedUrl("https://example.com/RPC2").parts(), limits: XmlRpcLimits());
let result = await rpc.result(XmlRpcCall(method: "sum", parameters: [XmlRpcInteger(2), XmlRpcInteger(3)]));
match result.kind() {
    case XmlRpcResultKind.success { result.value(); }
    case XmlRpcResultKind.fault { result.fault()::Fault::code; }
}

Description#

XML-RPC over HTTP: values, calls, a client and a handler.

Values are the XML-RPC types: int, boolean, string, double (kept as exact decimal text when read), dateTime.iso8601 (local, whole seconds), base64, array, struct and, when the limits allow it, nil. Everything read is bounded by XmlRpcLimits: depth 64, 4096 values, 1 MiB of text and 1 MiB of binary by default.

A server is an XmlRpcCalling behind XmlRpcHandling, which answers POSTs on one path; it returns XmlRpcSuccess(value) or XmlRpcFailure(XmlRpcFault(code:, message:)). Values show themselves to an XmlRpcWriting, one callback per kind. See examples/http/xmlrpc/greet.ok.
